title: Daily Health Briefing
intro: Good morning! Today's digest spans your five tracked topics — anti-aging, HIIT for women, pelvic floor training, integrative options for HER2+/TP53 breast cancer, and sleep. Highlights include a wave of newly launched rapamycin/rapalog aging trials, a fresh 19-RCT meta-analysis on HIIT in women, preoperative pelvic floor training that let ~43% of women postpone surgery, first-in-class p53 reactivator data for TP53-mutant tumors, and the largest placebo-controlled magnesium-for-sleep trial to date. Sources are linked as chips below each section. Informational only — discuss anything you'd act on with a clinician.

sections.body:
The big story this cycle is that rapamycin/rapalog research is finally moving from mouse to well-designed **human** trials — but nobody is claiming proven longevity yet.

- **A new generation of rapamycin trials just launched.** UT Health San Antonio (NIA-funded) opened the **RESTOR** study (NCT06658093) in March 2026 — up to 194 subjects (young controls plus adults 65–90) to pin down safe, effective doses and timing of **rapamycin (sirolimus)** and **everolimus**, notably testing whether optimal dosing differs by sex. The **RAP PAC** phase 1 (NCT05949658) is dose-finding weekly sirolimus/everolimus (5/10/15 mg) in adults 55–89. Wisconsin's **EVERLAST** (NCT05835999) — daily 0.5 mg vs weekly 5 mg everolimus in insulin-resistant older adults — reaches primary completion this month.
- **Bigger bets are coming.** ARPA-H's **PROSPR** program is funding a **$38M phase-3** hybrid trial (726 adults, one daily pill, ≥1 year) on intrinsic capacity, and the University of Arizona announced a **$12M**, 3-year rapamycin trial (physical function, frailty transition, IL-6) in adults 65+.
- **Urolithin A keeps building human data.** An NIH/NIA trial (NCT06274749) testing urolithin A on **glucose metabolism** in adults 55+ is slated to begin this month, adding to prior signals on muscle endurance and mitophagy.

Practical framing: the field is professionalizing, but off-label rapamycin for "anti-aging" remains **unproven** — dosing and safety are exactly what these new trials are trying to establish. Favor interventions with human RCTs and expect modest effects.

sections.body:
A brand-new meta-analysis sharpens the message: HIIT is a **cardio and body-composition** tool for women — but pair it with strength work for the rest.

- **New 19-RCT meta-analysis (middle-aged & older women).** Published in *Frontiers in Physiology* (searched through Nov 2025), HIIT produced a **large, high-certainty improvement in VO₂max** (SMD 1.20) versus controls, consistent across age, body-mass status, and program length. Walking ability improved borderline, but HIIT did **not** significantly improve **muscle strength, flexibility, or sit-to-stand** — so "HIIT alone is insufficient" for full functional fitness.
- **Long-term RCT reinforces the upside.** A 65-week supervised HIIT program (3×/week) in community-dwelling older women (*Women*, MDPI) significantly improved **aerobic capacity** (2-min step test), **lower-limb strength** (30-s chair stand), and **mobility** (Timed Up-and-Go), cut **body-fat %** and **visceral-fat index**, and raised quality of life — with **no major adverse events**.
- **For recreationally active younger women,** prior meta-analyses continue to show HIIT reliably improves cardiorespiratory fitness and lowers body-fat percentage (expect recomposition more than scale weight).

Bottom line: use HIIT 2–3×/week for the cardio/metabolic wins, **add resistance training** for strength and function, progress volume gradually, and keep recovery adequate.

sections.body:
**Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT)** stays first-line for stress urinary incontinence (SUI). This cycle's studies show it can *delay surgery*, *prevent* postpartum leakage, and work *better with biofeedback*.

- **Intensive training before surgery may make surgery unnecessary.** A March 2026 RCT in the *International Urogynecology Journal* (90 women awaiting mid-urethral sling) found **6 weeks of intensive preoperative PFMT** significantly improved muscle strength (Modified Oxford, d=0.85) and incontinence severity (d=0.90) versus education alone — and **43% postponed their planned surgery**.
- **Prevention works in pregnancy.** A large JAMA Network Open RCT (764 first-time mothers, 9 hospitals) found a structured **"PEFLOW" pelvic-floor workout** from 28 weeks' gestation cut SUI at 6 weeks postpartum (**8.7% vs 13.9%**) and more than doubled the share of women with strong pelvic floors (MOS ≥4).
- **Biofeedback boosts results.** A multicenter JAMA Network Open RCT (452 women with postpartum SUI) showed adding a **home pressure-mediated biofeedback device** to supervised PFMT roughly **doubled the cure rate (20.2% vs 8.7%)** and improved severity, strength, and adherence.

Key point: **correct technique + consistency beat sheer reps.** Confirm activation with a clinician or biofeedback; supervised (and biofeedback-assisted) programs generally outperform unsupervised ones.

sections.topic: Alternative & Integrative Options — HER2+ / TP53 (p53) Breast Cancer
sections.body:
"Alternative" is best read as **evidence-based integrative care alongside standard treatment** — never a replacement. Two threads stand out for TP53/p53-altered and HER2+ disease.

- **Directly drugging mutant p53.** The first-in-class oral **p53 reactivator rezatapopt (PC14586)** — selective for the **TP53 Y220C** mutation — is being tested in the phase-2 **PYNNACLE** basket trial (NCT04585750), and its phase-1 results were just published in *NEJM* (2026). Interim phase-2 data (Aug 2025 cutoff) showed a **33% overall response across 8 tumor types**, including an **18% response in the breast-cancer cohort**. It's investigational (KRAS wild-type only), with an NDA planned for 2027 — but it's a concrete example of turning a "p53 gene" mutation into a treatable target.
- **Supplements: mechanism vs proof.** A 2026 lab study reported that **cannabidiol (CBD)** reduced HER2 expression and induced apoptosis in HER2+ cells — mechanistically interesting, but **preclinical only**, not evidence to self-treat. Any supplement (CBD, curcumin, high-dose antioxidants) can **interact with HER2-targeted therapy**, so coordinate with your oncology team first.

Important framing: rezatapopt is genuine targeted science for p53-mutant cancers, while supplement data remain early. Use integrative options strictly as clinician-approved **add-ons**, not substitutes for HER2-directed therapy.

sections.body:
For restless or disjointed sleep, 2026 guidance keeps **behavioral therapy first**, with medications and supplements as measured add-ons.

- **CBT-I is still the anchor.** The AASM's 2026 clinical practice guideline (Apr 2026) concluded **CBT-I alone is the most efficacious first-line treatment**. Two conditional recommendations: CBT-I **plus** medication beats **medication alone**, but combination is **not** better than **CBT-I alone** — because CBT-I gives durable gains without drug risks. No single drug class emerged as the preferred add-on; among newer options, **dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs)** dampen arousal without much cognitive "hangover."
- **Magnesium — the largest trial yet.** A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (155 adults) found **magnesium bisglycinate (250 mg elemental Mg + ~1,523 mg glycine, daily × 28 days)** produced a **modest but significant** drop in Insomnia Severity Index vs placebo (effect size small, d≈0.2), with **bigger benefits in those with low dietary magnesium**.
- **Ashwagandha & melatonin.** A head-to-head RCT (200 adults) found **ashwagandha root extract** and **melatonin** each modestly improved sleep-onset latency and quality, with the **combination** performing best on total sleep time and efficiency. Adaptogen formulas also improved PSQI/restorative-sleep scores while lowering stress.

Best-practice habits for disjointed sleep:

1. Keep a **fixed wake time**, even on weekends.
2. Reserve the bed **for sleep only**; keep the room cool, dark, quiet.
3. Dim lights and cut screens during a wind-down window.
4. If disruption persists beyond a few weeks, see a provider to rule out **sleep apnea** and consider **CBT-I** (in-person or digital). Treat supplements as modest adjuncts, not cures.
